title: Retention Signal Matrix & SLA Guidelines
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, operational-first lexicon and quick-check KPI table for Customer Success QBRs and renewal conversations. It standardizes how we compute and present four primary retention signals: latency, uptime, cost-per-token, and cache-hit rate. It also includes measurement queries, alert heuristics, and a simple risk-weighting matrix to map metric regressions -> renewal conversation notes.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: CS leads, Solutions Eng, SRE oncall, account execs preparing QBR slides.
- Scope: hosted and dedicated customers (notes where private deployments differ).

Measurement conventions (applies to all metrics):
- Rolling windows: use 30d rolling for trend, 7d for recent drift, 24h for urgent alerts.
- Breakdowns: always show by route (API method), model (model_id / variant), region, and customer_tier (self-serve vs enterprise).
- Sample rate: production telemetry is sampled at request-level for latency/uptime; for very high-traffic customers show aggregated per-minute series to avoid noise.
- Baselines: use customer-specific baselines for targets where SLA exists; otherwise use platform recommended targets below.

Metric definitions and recommended platform queries (BigQuery / PromQL style pseudo):
1) Latency (observed response time)
- Definition: time between request received at ingress and final token emitted (end-to-end server-side latency), excluding client-side network latency. Report percentiles p50, p90, p95, p99.
- Measurement window: 7d (trend) and 30d (baseline).
- Example BigQuery: 
  SELECT
    APPROX_QUANTILES(lat_ms, 100)[OFFSET(95)] AS p95_ms,
    APPROX_QUANTILES(lat_ms, 100)[OFFSET(99)] AS p99_ms
  FROM `metrics.requests`
  WHERE customer_id = "CUST_123" AND _PARTITIONDATE BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 7 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE();
- Recommended targets (hosted): p95 < 700ms, p99 < 1.5s. For Dedicated / enterprise targets negotiated in contract.
- Alert heuristic: sustained p95 > 2x baseline for 30min -> SE/SRE engage.
- Notes: Include cold-start bucket and queued-time column where available; surface queuing% separately.

2) Uptime (availability)
- Definition: percentage of successful API responses (2xx) over total requests, excluding planned maintenance windows. Count gateway-level errors (5xx) and client-side rejections separately.
- Measurement window: 30d rolling for SLA measurement, 24h for incident detection.
- Example query: 
  SELECT
    SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(CASE WHEN status_code >= 200 AND status_code < 500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), COUNT(1)) * 100 AS availability_pct
  FROM `metrics.requests`
  WHERE customer_id = "CUST_123" AND _PARTITIONDATE BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE();
- SLA framing: e.g., 99.9% monthly availability -> allowed 43.8m downtime/month.
- Alert heuristic: availability < 99.5% over 24h -> incident review; < SLA over 7d -> escalation to account team.
- Notes: For private deployments, compute both control-plane and inference-plane availability separately.

3) Cost per 1k tokens (unit economics)
- Definition: total platform-infrastucture + model execution cost attributed to the customer divided by tokens generated (normalized to per-1,000 tokens). This may combine billed units and infrastructure depreciation/capacity costs for Dedicated customers.
- Formula (simple): cost_per_1k = (compute_cost + storage_cost + network_cost - credits) / (tokens_generated / 1000)
- Measurement window: monthly (billing cycle) and 30d rolling.
- Example data pull (pseudo SQL): 
  SELECT
    (SUM(infra_cost) + SUM(model_exec_cost) - SUM(credits)) / (SUM(tokens) / 1000) AS cost_per_1k
  FROM `billing.customer_costs`
  WHERE customer_id = "CUST_123" AND billing_period = '2026-02';
- Recommended targets: vary by model family; surfaced as benchmark table during QBR. Use cost trend + quality signal rather than raw absolute number.
- Alert heuristic: >20% month-over-month increase in cost_per_1k without corresponding usage growth or model change -> investigate prompt drift, increased unbounded generation, or model change.
- Notes: Include cache savings as line-item: effective_cost_per_1k = cost_per_1k * (1 - cache_token_savings).

4) Cache hit rate (behavioral + token-weighted)
- Definition: fraction of requests or tokens served from cache (prefix/KV cache, reranking cache) vs total tokens generated. Prefer token-weighted hit-rate because small cached responses and large generated answers should be weighted accordingly.
- Two variants to report: request-hit-rate = cached_requests / total_requests; token-hit-rate = cached_tokens / total_tokens. Report both.
- Measurement window: 30d rolling and 7d for recent regressions.
- Example query: 
  SELECT
    SUM(CASE WHEN cache_status = 'HIT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(1) AS request_hit_rate,
    SUM(CASE WHEN cache_status = 'HIT' THEN tokens ELSE 0 END) / SUM(tokens) AS token_hit_rate
  FROM `metrics.requests`
  WHERE customer_id = "CUST_123" AND _PARTITIONDATE BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE();
- Recommended targets: token_hit_rate > 25% for predictable workloads; request_hit_rate target depends on workload (e.g., assistant-like apps lower).
- Alert heuristic: sudden drop >10 percentage points in token_hit_rate vs 7d median -> check prompt changes, template edits, personalization flags.
- Notes: Show top-10 prefixes that lost hits and top-10 routes by lost token-savings.

Supplemental KPIs to include in QBR table (short list):
- Error rate (5xx/total)
- Throughput (req/sec at peak)
- Median cost per inference (if we report per-request)
- Quality regressions (human-evaluated failures or eval-run alerts)

Compact KPI table (copyable into QBR slides)
Columns: KPI | Definition | Measurement window | Platform target (recommended) | Alert threshold | Owner
1) Latency p95 | end-to-end server-side p95 | 7d / 30d | <700ms hosted | p95 > 2x baseline for 30min | SRE / CS Ops
2) Uptime (%) | successful responses / total | 30d | >=99.9% (if SLA) | <99.5% over 24h | SRE / Account Eng
3) Cost per 1k tokens | infra+exec / (tokens/1000) | monthly | customer-benchmarked | +20% MoM w/o usage growth | Finance + CS Ops
4) Token-weighted cache hit rate | cached_tokens / total_tokens | 30d | >25% (predictable apps) | -10pp vs 7d median | Solutions Eng + CS
5) Error rate (5xx%) | server errors / total | 7d | <0.2% | >0.5% 1h spike | SRE

Risk-weighting and renewal signal mapping (simple heuristic):
- Green: all KPIs within targets OR any single metric mildly outside (<=10% deviation) but improving -> low risk.
- Amber: one major metric outside target (e.g., p95 > 2x baseline or cost +20% MoM) or two minor metrics trending worse -> medium risk (prepare action plan).
- Red: sustained multi-metric regression (>=2 major metrics) or uptime below SLA -> high risk (engage AE + Solutions + Exec sponsor).

Actionable steps for CS before QBR (checklist):
- Pull 30d and 7d KPI snapshots and include time-series sparkline for each metric.
- Run prefix-level cache diagnostic and include top 5 cache-miss causes.
- If cost increased >10% MoM, include token-distribution histogram (long tail free-text prompts).
- Pre-run a quality eval on a small prompt set if latency or model changes are visible.
- Prepare a one-slide remediation plan with owners and ETA for any Amber/Red items.

Templates and snippets (copy/paste)
- One-line metric callout for slides: "Customer X: p95 latency 650ms (7d), uptime 99.92% (30d), cost/1k $3.42 (month), token-hit-rate 28% (30d). No regressions in eval set."
- Escalation note subject line: "[Action Req] sustained p95 regression for Customer X — recommend SE + SRE sync"

Differences for Dedicated & Private deployments:
- Dedicated: cost attribution should include committed capacity amortization; show nominal vs effective cost per 1k at current utilization. Cache behavior may differ if customers host their own cache layer.
- Private (on-prem): surface both control-plane (we may still get heartbeats) and inference-plane metrics; acceptance criteria often contract-defined — always align with legal/contract.

Open questions / items to finalize (for CS ops):
- Agree canonical BigQuery table names and columns for telemetry (SRE item).
- Decide which cost components are included in cost_per_1k for Dedicated customers (finance item).
- Add an automated QBR export template in the console (product idea).

Owners and next steps:
